component.name: jolt
component.title: JOLT
component.description: Transform JSON to JSON with a JOLT specification.
component.label: transformation

allowTemplateFromHeader.description: Whether the endpoints read the CamelJoltResourceUri and CamelJoltContext headers. It is the default of the allowTemplateFromHeader option of each endpoint. Enable it only when the headers come from a trusted source.

contentCache.description: Whether the endpoints keep the content of their spec resource in memory after the first read. It is the default of the contentCache option of each endpoint. Each endpoint builds its JOLT transform from the spec once, at the first exchange, and keeps it, so false does not make it read a changed spec again.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

transform.label: advanced
transform.description: A JOLT Transform that all endpoints of the component use in place of the transform that they build from their spec. When set, the endpoints do not read their spec resource, and transformDsl and the CamelJoltResourceUri header have no effect. To use the CamelJoltContext header, it must also be a ContextualTransform, such as a Chainr.

CamelJoltResourceUri.description: The URI of the spec resource to use instead of the resourceUri of the endpoint, in the same form, such as classpath:, file: or http:. The producer reads it only when allowTemplateFromHeader is true, and removes it from the message. It then uses the endpoint with the same options for that URI.

CamelJoltContext.description: A Map of values that the modify-overwrite-beta, modify-default-beta and modify-define-beta operations of the spec can refer to with a caret followed by the key. The producer reads it only when allowTemplateFromHeader is true. The transform must take a context: of the transformDsl types only Chainr does, and the others fail the exchange.

producerIn.description: Parsed JSON (a Map or a List), or JSON as text, bytes, a stream, a file or a Jackson JsonNode, which is parsed. Text that does not start with { or [ reaches the spec as it is. With inputType=JsonString the body is always parsed as JSON

producerOut.description: The JSON the spec makes: a Map for an object, a List for an array; JSON text with outputType=JsonString

resourceUri.description: Path to the resource. You can prefix with: classpath, file, http, ref, or bean. classpath, file and http loads the resource using these protocols (classpath is default). ref will lookup the resource in the registry. bean will call a method on a bean to be used as the resource. For bean you can specify the method name after dot, eg bean:myBean.myMethod.

allowTemplateFromHeader.description: Whether the producer reads the CamelJoltResourceUri and CamelJoltContext headers. If false, the producer ignores both headers. Enable it only when the headers come from a trusted source.

contentCache.description: Sets whether to use resource content cache or not

inputType.description: Whether the producer parses the body as JSON or uses it as it is. With Hydrated, a body that is JSON text (its first non-whitespace character is { or [), bytes, a stream or a file is parsed as JSON, and any other body, such as a Map or a List, is used as it is. With JsonString, the body is always parsed as JSON. With both types, a Jackson JsonNode body is converted to a Map or a List.

outputType.description: Whether the producer sets the body to the result of the transform as it is or to its JSON text. With Hydrated, the body is the result as it is, which is a Map for a JSON object and a List for a JSON array. With JsonString, the body is the result written as a JSON String.

transformDsl.description: The JOLT transform that the producer builds from the spec of resourceUri. Chainr: the spec is a JSON array of operations, each with an operation name (such as shift, default, remove, sort, cardinality or modify-overwrite-beta) and its spec. Shiftr, Defaultr and Removr: the spec of that one operation. Sortr: sorts the keys of the JSON objects and reads no spec. Not used when the transform option of the component is set.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.
